summary: The Approve locator of the request details page object is ambiguous (strict mode violation); an exact name match fixes the test code without changing any assertion.

diagnosis.explanation: Both attempts fail in RequestDetailsPage.approve with a strict mode violation: getByRole('button', { name: 'Approve' }) matches two buttons. The locator, not the application, is ambiguous; the requirement under test (REQ-005) is not contradicted.

alternatives.explanation: If an "Approve all" button is not expected on the details page, the extra control would be an application change for human triage.

missingEvidence: A screenshot or trace of the details page at the time of failure.
recommendedInvestigation: Confirm in the UI whether an "Approve all" control is intended on the request details page.

changes.rationale: Match the Approve button by its exact accessible name, so it no longer also matches "Approve all".

repair.impact: Only RequestDetailsPage.approveButton changes; every test that approves through the page object uses the exact name.
repair.expectedBehaviorPreserved: The approval workflow (CAN-004) still clicks the Approve button and asserts the same statuses in UI and API; no assertion changes.
risks: If the visible name of the Approve button changes, the exact match fails loudly instead of matching another control.
validationSteps: After human H7 authorization, run the targeted test: npx playwright test --grep @TC-005-08
Review the diff of the page object before approving at H3.

assumptions.statement: The second button belongs to the application under test.
assumptions.impact: If it does not, the diagnosis would be environment-related.

findings.message: The evidence is a report excerpt only; no trace was supplied.
